gloss: to giggle; to snicker; to titter

definitions.gloss: to giggle; to snicker; to titter
definitions.explanation: to laugh quietly in a suppressed way, often behind one's hand

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちがくすくす{笑|わら}っている。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{口|くち}を{手|て}で{隠|かく}しながらくすくす{笑|わら}った。
examples.english: She giggled while covering her mouth with her hand.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}の{言|い}い{間違|まちが}いに、クラス{中|じゅう}がくすくす{笑|わら}いを{漏|も}らした。
examples.english: The whole class let out stifled giggles at the teacher's slip of the tongue.

notes:
Combines the onomatopoeia くすくす (the sound of stifled laughter) with {笑|わら}う (to laugh). Describes quiet, suppressed laughing — lighter and more restrained than outright laughter.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- くすくす{笑|わら}いを{漏|も}らす: to let out a giggle
- くすくす{笑|わら}い{出|だ}す: to start giggling
- くすくす{笑|わら}い{声|ごえ}: the sound of giggling

SIMILAR WORDS:
- にやにや{笑|わら}う: to grin — smiling in a knowing or smug way, without sound
- げらげら{笑|わら}う: to guffaw — loud, unrestrained laughter
- くすっと{笑|わら}う: to chuckle — a single brief, quiet laugh
- {忍|しの}び{笑|わら}い: stifled laugh — trying to hold back laughter

NOTE: くすくす can have a slightly negative nuance when it implies laughing at someone behind their back.
